Ring Lardner, Short Fiction.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ring-lardner/short-fiction

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ring Lardner, the annotator, died 1933 (Wikidata death date).

First publication of the text used: between 1914 and 1930 (SE colophon: 'Short Fiction was compiled from short stories and novellas published between 1914 and 1930 by Ring Lardner').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's rights statement (quoted below) says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (the facts do not establish the country of first publication, and the text was first published between 1914 and 1930; the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less for these people. The last person to die, Ring Lardner, died in 1933, so that term ended on 31 December 2003 at the latest.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: Short Fiction was compiled from short stories and novellas published between 1914 and 1930 by Ring Lardner.
- Wikidata Q919515 (Ring Lardner), P570 = 1933-09-25
